extName.description: The extension's name. Keep it as it is in every language.

extDescription.message: Small tools for everyday work. First: each Google Docs, Sheets or Slides file shows its Drive folder path next to the title.
extDescription.description: The Chrome Web Store summary and the chrome://extensions description. At most 132 characters.

actionTitle.description: Tooltip of the toolbar icon; clicking it opens the options page.

localeCode.description: The code of this language (en, es, ko, ja). Do not translate: the extension reads it back.

commonFactJoin.description: Puts two short facts side by side on one line. $1 and $2 are the facts.

pathMyDrive.description: The first step of a folder path for a file in the person's own Drive. Use Google Drive's own name for it.

pathSharedDrive.description: Stands in for a shared drive whose name could not be read. Use Google Drive's own term.

pathUntitled.description: Stands in for a folder whose name is empty.

pathHidden.description: Shown next to a document's title when its Drive folder cannot be seen by the signed-in account.

pathOwner.description: Follows pathHidden on the same line. $1 is the file owner's display name. Lowercase in English because it follows a dot separator.

pathHiddenTitle.message: The file is not in a folder your account can open, for example because it was shared with you.

pathShowButton.description: Button next to a document's title. Clicking it opens Google sign-in, then shows the file's Drive folder path. Keep it short.

pathShowTitle.message: Sign in with Google to show this file's Drive folder. Übermensch reads file and folder names only.

pathNotConfigured.description: Shown next to a document's title in a build without a Google sign-in client. Keep it short.

pathNotConfiguredTitle.message: This copy of Übermensch has no Google sign-in client, so the Drive folder cannot be read.

pathLoading.description: Shown briefly while the folder path is being read.

pathError.description: Button shown when the folder path could not be read; clicking it tries again. Keep it short.

pathErrorTitle.message: The folder could not be read: $1. Click to try again.
pathErrorTitle.description: Tooltip of pathError. $1 is the reason, one of the error* messages.

pathWrongAccount.description: Button shown when the account chosen in Google sign-in is not the one the open document uses; clicking it opens sign-in again. Keep it short.

pathWrongAccountTitle.message: Choose the account this document is open in. Click to sign in again.

pathFullTitle.description: Tooltip of the whole folder path. $1 is the full path, folder names separated by ›.

pathPartialTitle.message: Folders above the first one shown are not visible to your account.
pathPartialTitle.description: Added to the tooltip, and the tooltip of the leading …, when the top of the path cannot be seen.

pathOpenInDrive.description: Tooltip of one folder in the path. $1 is the folder's name.

errorNetwork.message: Google Drive could not be reached
errorNetwork.description: Reason inside pathErrorTitle when there is no connection or Drive did not answer.

errorUnknown.description: Reason inside pathErrorTitle for any other failure. Lowercase in English because it follows a colon.

optionsTitle.description: Heading and tab title of the options page.

optionsDrivePathHeading.description: Heading of the options page section about the folder path feature.

optionsDrivePathLead.message: Shows the Drive folder of the open Docs, Sheets or Slides file next to its title, each folder a link. Only file and folder names are read, never the content.
optionsDrivePathLead.description: Explains the folder path feature under its heading.

optionsDocsAccess.description: Label of the switch that grants the extension access to docs.google.com.

optionsDocsAccessTitle.message: Lets Übermensch add the folder path to docs.google.com pages. Chrome asks you first.

optionsDocsAccessOn.message: On: the path shows next to the title of Docs, Sheets and Slides files.
optionsDocsAccessOn.description: State line under the switch while access is granted.

optionsDocsAccessOff.message: Off: nothing runs on Google Docs.
optionsDocsAccessOff.description: State line under the switch while access is not granted.

optionsAccessRefused.message: Chrome did not grant access to Google Docs.
optionsAccessRefused.description: Shown when the person declined Chrome's permission prompt.

optionsNotConfigured.message: Google sign-in is not configured in this copy of Übermensch, so the folder path cannot be read yet.
optionsNotConfigured.description: Shown on the options page in a build without a Google sign-in client.

optionsAccountsHeading.description: Heading of the list of Google accounts signed in for the folder path.

optionsAccountsNone.message: No account is signed in. Click Show folder next to a document's title to sign in.
optionsAccountsNone.description: Shown when no account is signed in. Quote the pathShowButton text as it is in this language.

optionsAccountUntil.message: Signed in until $1, or until Chrome closes
optionsAccountUntil.description: Under an account's address. $1 is a time of day.

optionsSignOut.description: Button that forgets one account's sign-in on this device.

optionsSignOutTitle.message: Forget the sign-in of $1 on this device
optionsSignOutTitle.description: Tooltip of optionsSignOut. $1 is the account's e-mail address.

optionsClearCache.description: Button that forgets the folder names kept for a few minutes.

optionsClearCacheTitle.message: Folder names are kept in memory for a few minutes; clear them to read them from Drive again

optionsPrivacyLink.description: Footer link to the privacy policy.

optionsSupportLink.description: Footer link to the support page.
